Revision2 specifies existing ProductionEvidenceAdapter/TrustedInspectionReceipt unknown evidence representation, partial completeness and limitation, preserving stored TESTS outcome unions and historical results; adds direct code citations. summary.prose: Make the existing review engine usable through a small native reviewer interface. The host handles identity and coverage bookkeeping, saves assessed work promptly, returns useful incomplete results, and presents one operational activation decision backed by real review evidence. The first rollout proves Claude source-only review and resume while keeping existing safeguards and the durable kernel.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a1: a daemon-owned durable investigation state machine with provider-independent accepted state. Seed each run with sc1's approved tasks/checks, artifact references and explicit commit packets, not embedded source partitions. Source-only and indexed-impact runs use identical packets, obligations, reviewer policy and completion checks; only the indexed capability in sc3 differs. Substantive judgments remain the independent agent's job; deterministic guards validate identity, evidence provenance, coverage and publication, not semantic correctness. Reuse existing LLMProvider/CliProvider read-only execution, budget admission, source freshness, ownership and canonical artifact lifecycle; introduce the investigation protocol and durable accepted-state store behind the existing code-review entrypoints. Checkpoint cadence is per reviewed commit-packet block, independently of continuation boundaries and run time limits; multiple block checkpoints may be accepted within one managed reviewer session.

boundary.internal: Private implementation of s7: Make scoped reviews usable with simple assessments and durable progress

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own subject preparation, attribution ambiguity detection, exact Git commit/blob/block navigation and frozen context binding. Define foundational runtime-port types only; do not implement task investigation, a recovery store or new accounting storage. No generic HEAD/working-tree diff may select scope.

Own required-row enumeration, evidence identity/provenance and coverage relationships/dispositions. Reuse subject inputs and runtime ports. Keep ledger validation helpers private; do not execute reviewer turns or publish CRs.

Own independent read-only task-directed continuation behavior, on-demand source navigation, optional indexed caller/impact enrichment, budget admission, bounded retry/pause and attempt usage emission through foundational ports. In-memory ports are test scaffolding while production selection remains disabled until s4/s6; no durable storage implementation or terminal approval logic. Publish and acknowledge incremental block progress within continuations, with partial cross-block assessments recorded rather than lost. Domain progress contracts only; no competing MCP phase/schema ownership. External registration belongs to s6.

Own durable implementation of foundational acceptance/usage-outbox ports, append/replay/checkpoint integrity, lease/generation fencing, uncertain attempts and compatibility/time recovery. Do not alter review criteria or introduce a usage warehouse. Its recovery implementation is composed by downstream s6 rather than consumed backwards by s3. Persist/replay block-level evidence and assessment receipts independently of final provider-call completion.

Own completion coverage/freshness/party validation, canonical CR adaptation and idempotent terminal publication receipts. Reuse existing lifecycle and severity/confidence policy. Do not let a completion request, missing evidence or a failed run masquerade as a completed verdict.

Own production composition, equivalent MCP/daemon/controller start/status/resume/cancel adapters, status/usage presentation fields, explicit engine rollout/rollback, legacy compatibility and evaluation fixtures. No client opens stores directly; no client-specific board UI or design-review replacement. Sole new-engine MCP adapter/schema owner; reconcile 8315a11f/S005 legacy sc7 as specified in the architecture and record code-only supersession before opt-in. Verify routing partitions across both installation orders.

nonFunctional.performance: No eager whole-source or whole-contract repetition and no mandatory call-per-clause. Bounded read ranges and explicit evidence references prevent unbounded request growth.128K inclusive estimated admission and five-minute continuation cap; default120active-minute/24continuation limits pause with durable progress and explicit extension rather than claim success. Use deterministic/mock providers for routine tests; measure authorized live comparisons against recorded baselines before claiming savings. Block checkpoint acceptance is independent of run duration:120minutes is a pause ceiling, never a save interval. Grouping several block assessments in one session remains allowed.
nonFunctional.security: Daemon owns runtime state and DB access; cloud access remains LLMProvider/CliProvider only. Independent reviewer identity is checked at start and publication. Source reads are pinned and read-only; untrusted repository text is data, not tool/policy authority. Trusted evidence reads cannot escape the declared snapshot/approved-artifact view, graph queries bind to the registered source repo and declared dependency closure, and native adapters that cannot meet pinning/read-only capability refuse explicitly. Private runtime state uses restrictive access; metadata diagnostics contain no raw prompts/evidence.
nonFunctional.observability: Expose run/subject/engine/policy IDs, owner generation, attempt lifecycle, required/covered/unverified rows, pause/stale causes and resume compatibility. Show managed attempt count/active time, observed usage quality and unknown/pending observations distinctly from reservations and estimates. Emit status/heartbeats without replaying accepted work; transport disconnect is not a review verdict. Keep human-readable review reports only in /tmp. Surface latest accepted block/progress receipt and outstanding block IDs so clients can distinguish durable block progress from provider-session liveness.
nonFunctional.durability: Journal-committed acceptance precedes acknowledgment; snapshots/checkpoints are reconstructible and verified against immutable evidence/answer blobs. Detect torn tails and corruption, fence concurrent owners and late replies, preserve uncertain provider outcomes and idempotent completion/usage receipts. Pauses do not erase consumed execution time. Legacy runs are explicitly non-resumable; runtime data remains outside artifact JSON and excluded from changed scope. Every reviewed block is journal-committed before its durable acknowledgment and cursor advancement, even while a native session continues. Accepted block state survives an uncertain or failed enclosing attempt; only unfinished/unacknowledged work is resumed.

dataModelChanges.details: Private non-durable transport only, versioned separately from the unchanged public/domain engine-v1 commands. review_read accepts a typed target: change(blockId, before|after, optional bounded subrange), context(repo-relative path, inclusive range), artifact(subject artifact id, range), or test(task id). The host supplies all revisions. An absent changed side returns an explicit absence result and no fabricated source receipt; wider source must use context. review_progress accepts blockId, disposition, evidence aliases, explicit expectation assessments/findings, notes and unresolved refs. review_reply accepts finish|yield and a reason, with no new assessment deltas. The child MCP server validates shape; the authenticated parent translates to existing domain operations before any action.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: type ReviewModelProtocol = 'bound-v1' | 'compact-v1'; type CompactFinalAck = { acknowledged: true }; type ReviewToolError = { code: string; message: string; hint?: string; referenceDigest?: string; retryable: boolean };

dataModelChanges.details: A projection of the existing run basis/state, not a second ledger. Detailed approved tasks/checks remain available; packet metadata covers the full selected scope. The host suggests one pending block and shows its applicable expectation groups. Short evidence/expectation aliases resolve only through the current host binding; identities, subject hashes, generation, sequence, findings IDs and receipt IDs are generated or copied by the host. Grouping changes presentation only: explicit member assessments expand to existing authoritative rows and pass all current provenance/test/applicability validation. Cross-file context reads stay available. Tool results expose remainingMs and accepted progress; at the soft-yield threshold, new focus is refused with a corrective yield instruction while current assessment/finish can still be accepted until the unchanged hard cap. No timer invents a semantic judgment.

dataModelChanges.entity: Canonical BUILD review scope and TESTS metadata
dataModelChanges.details: Reuse the existing canonical BUILD as the normal scope source. A daemon-generated reviewScope records full source commit, exact commit/parent identities, attributed block IDs, task provenance and unresolved ambiguity. It is captured from the existing tracked build change set; trailers alone do not establish exclusive hunk ownership, and mixed/unprovable blocks require explicit selection. The review start selects this exact versioned manifest, which is pinned before dispatch. Existing separately approved ISSUE scope references remain readable. The host rejects arbitrary caller booleans or mutable scope. BUILD/TESTS writes preserve canonical repo identity and history; stored abbreviated Git IDs are uniquely resolved and audited as the same object. Old test evidence remains unknown when it cannot be bound to the reviewed source; metadata repair never turns it into pass. Representation clarification [c7,c8]: unknown is an existing derived review-evidence result, not a new persisted TESTS case outcome. Keep TestCaseResult, TestRecordFile.titles[].result, testsPassed and historical per-Task commit/ranAt/results unchanged. ProductionEvidenceAdapter compares each recorded Task commit with the pinned BUILD source (after unique same-object OID normalization) and uses verifiedTaskResult only for matching source. Otherwise its existing TrustedInspectionReceipt.testResult is unknown, with completeness partial and an explicit source-binding limitation. This receipt is admitted and persisted through the existing evidence/checkpoint kernel; TESTS is not rewritten to unknown and metadata repair cannot upgrade evidence. Missing or foreign canonical TESTS identity/integrity still refuses inspection. No new provenance field or test-result union is required for this behavior.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: No TestCaseResult or TestRecordFile.titles[].result change. Existing review receipt: TrustedInspectionReceipt.testResult: 'pass' | 'fail' | 'skipped' | 'unknown' | null; ReviewReadReceiptV1.completeness: 'complete' | 'partial' | 'unavailable'; limitations: readonly string[]. TESTS meta.repoPath is additive canonical metadata; retain each Task's commit, ranAt and original results. New BUILD.body.reviewScope is the separate additive scope manifest described above.

dataModelChanges.details: Keep real installed probe replay, current native policy checks and existing runtime evidence. Separate native boundary identity from broad engine release/source provenance: exact CLI/runtime images, versioned adapter, model-facing catalog/final schema, resolved launch/config/permissions, private bridge/binding/auth code and isolation-policy inputs define the reviewed boundary manifest. Changes to those inputs invalidate proof and require the real paired native probe. Host authorization/provenance negative checks are rerun deterministically against current code. Ordinary orchestration, reporting, grouping or workflow-document changes do not by themselves require another model isolation pair. Reviewed subject source/contracts and run policy/schema compatibility remain pinned separately; inability to establish the narrow boundary fails closed. The first compact adapter requires a new proof; the previous v2 record is historical evidence only.

dataModelChanges.entity: Consolidated activation decision and result projection
dataModelChanges.details: Use one canonical record of an existing supported artifact kind for explicit default-activation signoff, not one approval per probe/oracle/evaluation fixture. It references the actual qualified backend/mode/boundary, completed implementation/test/code-review evidence, actual known-defect/clean/cross-file review results and receipt IDs, recovery/ownership outcomes, limitations and existing predecessor reconciliation. Approval comes from canonical lifecycle history, never an approved:true field. A bounded explicit pilot is authorized by the normal approved workflow/user action and availability switch while the default remains legacy; default use also needs the activation decision. Inconclusive reports are regenerable /tmp projections of accepted checkpoints with findings and unresolved work, not new successful CR artifacts. Run->checkpoint/evidence ownership remains unchanged; one activation decision references one or more independently ready backend/mode capabilities and owns none of their evidence. Default changes and later legacy CODE deletion remain separate explicit decisions.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: S7 is a private facade and operational integration consumer of the S6-owned entrypoint/status/rollout boundary. It does not implement a replacement shared contract, state machine, evidence ledger, recovery store or publisher. The native private protocol is normalized into unchanged domain commands; incomplete reports are status projections and never bypass sc5 complete-CR validation. A local consumer declaration is proposed because the generated addStory boundary omitted it.

errorCases.scenario: Invalid, missing or absent-side source reference
errorCases.detection: Host checks the typed target against the admitted packet, real side spans and bounded revision contents before reading.
errorCases.response: Return a safe typed error with a valid target example or context-read hint; absence is explicit, never a fabricated 1–1 range. Log operation, error code and reference digest only.
errorCases.userImpact: Reviewer can correct navigation without guessing opaque IDs.

errorCases.scenario: Caller attempts unauthorized path, foreign owner or expired binding
errorCases.detection: Existing broker peer, binding and scope validators reject the request before translation or IO.
errorCases.response: Refuse without exposing source or credentials; require the legitimate owner to resume or re-admit through existing sc7.
errorCases.userImpact: No evidence from another run is accepted.

errorCases.scenario: Two requests race or a progress acknowledgement is lost
errorCases.detection: Existing owner fencing, serialized dispatch and durable acceptance sequence detect contention or a previously accepted operation.
errorCases.response: Return existing typed busy/stale/idempotent outcome. Re-read accepted checkpoint state before resending; never create a parallel reviewer or infer acceptance from a timeout.
errorCases.userImpact: Durable work survives reconnect without duplicate coverage.

errorCases.scenario: Unprovable commit attribution or stale source/test provenance
errorCases.detection: Canonical BUILD scope validation checks exact commit and parent objects, selected blocks and current artifact revisions; TESTS evidence checks its recorded source binding.
errorCases.response: Block ambiguous review admission and request explicit scope selection. Treat unbound historical tests as unknown, preserving historical results; do not certify them through metadata repair.
errorCases.userImpact: Operator sees the precise missing scope or evidence requirement.

errorCases.detection: Adoption compares the installed CLI/runtime, compact adapter/catalog/final schema, launch permissions, broker/auth/isolation code and their security-relevant dependency/configuration closure with the qualified manifest.
errorCases.response: Fail closed for that backend/mode. Requalify that boundary once; unknown closure is not exempted. Ordinary subject source freshness remains checked separately.
errorCases.userImpact: Existing qualification cannot silently authorize a changed execution boundary.

errorCases.scenario: Reviewer reaches soft yield or hard execution deadline
errorCases.detection: Host reports remaining monotonic deadline budget; at 60 seconds remaining it stops offering a new focus block. Existing hard deadline remains authoritative.
errorCases.response: Allow acknowledgement of the current assessment and explicit yield until the hard cap; then cancel/drain via existing lifecycle. Preserve accepted checkpoints and emit an inconclusive status report. No new 90-second watchdog, invented assessment or automatic full retry.
errorCases.userImpact: Partial work is visible and resumable; incomplete work cannot approve a BUILD.

errorCases.scenario: Finish requested with unresolved obligations or no accepted reply
errorCases.detection: Existing completion assessor finds missing rows, unsupported findings or unfinished blocks; native final acknowledgement lacks a host-accepted terminal reply.
errorCases.response: Project grouped unresolved obligations to /tmp and retain resumable status; no complete CR or automatic approval. A native zero exit alone is insufficient.
errorCases.userImpact: Reviewer/operator receives useful partial results without false success.

errorCases.scenario: Default activation requested without canonical user approval
errorCases.detection: Existing adoption admission resolves the single activation decision's canonical history and qualified backend/mode, not a caller-provided approved boolean.
errorCases.response: Refuse default activation. An explicitly requested bounded pilot may run only with availability enabled and all mechanical scope/isolation prerequisites met; default stays legacy.
errorCases.userImpact: Real verification is possible before the one final activation decision.

errorCases.detection: Strict private wire-version parsing rejects incompatible compact messages; workflow gate detects an unapproved sc7 consumer amendment or incompatible upstream signature.
errorCases.response: Keep old admitted runs on their bound protocol and status reader; require supported resume or cancellation. Block S7 build until the local dependency amendment is approved; never coerce old proof into compact-v1.
errorCases.userImpact: Compatibility and design ownership remain explicit.

migration.stateBefore: s1 bundles c1/c2/c3 locate the existing native catalog and broker, sc7 orchestration with durable kernel, and TESTS writer. The actual failed acceptance performed reads but accepted no block; old qualification is for the existing protocol. Default remains legacy; earlier failed acceptance records remain failed.
migration.stateAfter: One compact private reviewer facade consumes unchanged sc7/domain contracts, uses real source targets and host-owned durable acknowledgements, exposes complete or inconclusive results honestly, and has installed-Claude/source-only acceptance evidence. Default activation is available only after one separate explicit approval of a canonical ISSUE decision; legacy code deletion remains later work.

migrationSteps.action: After LLD and local sc7 consumer amendment approval, implement the minimal compact bridge, typed targets/errors, host-owned assessment translation and focused view. Validate with deterministic bridge/evidence regressions. Keep existing default legacy and existing bound protocol readers.

Add narrow execution-boundary manifest comparison and explicit qualified pilot admission, separating availability from default engine selection. Introduce a versioned compact adapter qualification (proposed claude-scoped-v3; never relabel v2 evidence). Capture fresh installed CLI inventory and active hook/plugin/instruction canary proof once for the changed boundary. Run a serial bounded pilot on an exact canonical subject and require an actual durable block ACK before proceeding. If it fails, diagnose that run and fix this slice rather than building more acceptance bureaucracy.
prerequisiteFlags: Availability enabled for explicit pilot only

migrationSteps.action: Complete concise member-wise expectation grouping, accepted-state inconclusive reports, canonical BUILD reviewScope capture and TESTS metadata/provenance preservation. Route new normal starts through configured engine; keep existing sessions on their bound engine. Validate exact scope and completion behavior with focused tests.

Integrate existing restart/cancel/ownership/freshness behavior with the facade and prove compatibility, soft yield and hard-disable cancellation/drain. Reuse the existing journal and completion assessor; no replacement recovery framework or proof conversion.

Run serial installed-Claude/source-only known-defect, clean and cross-file reviews plus cancel-after-ACK/resume and concurrent-session acceptance. Reuse accepted checkpoints when supported; do not repeat all live tests absent a changed prerequisite or failed assertion. Record actual outcomes, elapsed time and available usage; unknown model counts/tokens remain unknown. Assemble one canonical ISSUE activation decision draft with evidence references and limitations. Task acceptance excludes final Story review, BUILD approval and activation.

After all implementation Tasks are validated, perform the independent final Story code review and request human BUILD completion approval. Then present the single activation decision for explicit user approval; activate only the evidenced backend/mode. This is post-Task workflow, not an extra Task prerequisite. Retain legacy code until a later explicit deletion decision.

If operator disables availability or rolls back default, refuse new investigation turns, cancel/drain according to existing lifecycle, retain readable checkpoints and final reports, and select legacy for new default reviews. Never resume an old run through a different engine.

migration.backwardCompat: Public domain v1, sc7 signatures, existing checkpoint ownership and complete-CR publication remain authoritative. Compact-v1 is a separately validated private native transport; bound-v1 admitted sessions retain their original route and readers. Unsupported native versions fail explicitly with status/cancel available. Existing qualification is historical and cannot qualify the changed catalog/schema. New BUILD scope metadata is additive; older artifacts need a provable explicit scope, not broad HEAD fallback. Preserve historical TESTS results without certifying unbound source evidence. No bulk artifact rewrite, new artifact kind, signing keys or new persistence substrate.

alternativesConsidered.name: Thin native reviewer facade over the existing host kernel
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the native agent session and current durable domain; present compact reads and assessments, with protocol bookkeeping performed by the host.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The dedicated review MCP surface accepts human-sized source requests and block assessments. The existing host integration translates them to current bound read/progress/reply operations and computes identities, sequences, coverage-row expansion and receipts. Accepted checkpoints, leases, scoped source and canonical publication remain the existing kernel's authority. The operator sees one capability/activation decision backed by actual test and native-boundary evidence, with an explicit bounded pilot distinct from changing the default.
pros: Reuses the working scoped reads and all existing ownership/recovery/publication machinery.
Removes model bookkeeping while preserving mandatory validation and prompt per-block durable acceptance.
Keeps the existing engine and external status/run identity; no new storage or provider-authoritative recovery.
cons: The private native catalog/launch qualification changes once and needs a real compatibility probe.
The host must map compact assessment IDs to precise existing ledger obligations without dropping uncertainty.

alternativesConsidered.name: Host-driven structured action turns
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use serial structured CLI replies selecting reads or assessments, with the host executing each action against the current scoped kernel.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A host action coordinator asks the existing CLI structured-output provider for the next evidence requests, block assessments or yield. It executes all reads through current pinned adapters, accepts block results through current durable progress, and returns only needed results for the next turn. Related actions can be selected together and global pending coverage remains host-owned; no fixed source chunks or call-per-clause schedule is prescribed. Existing storage and completion remain unchanged, but the native agent/MCP interaction is replaced by a new action envelope.
pros: The host directly controls action sequencing, bounded turns and checkpoint scheduling.
Uses the existing structured CLI provider and durable kernel rather than private provider conversation recovery.
cons: Adds a second execution coordinator and new action-envelope compatibility work.
More CLI invocations and repeated conversation material may recreate the overhead this epic is meant to reduce; accuracy/consumption would need new evidence.
Changes substantially more of the already-working execution boundary before a successful pilot.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Could meet core guarantees through existing ports, but introduces a second coordinator and more compatibility/provider-turn behavior before validating the current native path.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: Shows the changed reviewer/host boundary: semantic assessments become durable kernel checkpoints before another block is suggested. Incomplete work stays resumable, and default activation follows a separate human decision.

messages.description: Explicit pilot does not change the default; host verifies exact subject and mechanical admission.

messages.label: Tasks + exact packet metadata + focus block
messages.description: Host omits opaque bookkeeping and full empty rows while keeping all selected scope discoverable.

messages.label: Read changed span / pinned context
messages.description: Strict typed targets allow cross-file evidence; safe typed errors explain invalid navigation.

messages.label: Evidence alias + time remaining
messages.description: Only scoped, revision-bound evidence is returned; host owns authoritative identities.

messages.label: Assess block and explicit expectation members
messages.description: Reviewer supplies semantic judgments and evidence aliases, not run hashes or sequence bookkeeping.

messages.label: Translate and validate bound progress
messages.description: Existing authoritative ledger and provenance validators remain unchanged.

messages.label: Durable accepted checkpoint
messages.description: Journal commit precedes acknowledgement; concurrent/stale owners cannot accept work.

messages.label: ACK + next focus or yield
messages.description: Accepted work survives cancellation; at soft yield no new focus is offered.

messages.label: Finish or yield
messages.description: No new assessment delta is smuggled into the terminal request; native final ACK alone is not completion.

messages.label: Assess completion or retain pause
messages.description: Only complete validated coverage may publish CR; unresolved work yields an inconclusive /tmp status projection.

messages.label: Resume accepted work / later approve activation
messages.description: Resume retains single ownership. After Task validation, final Story review and BUILD approval, one canonical activation decision is presented separately.

Catalog changes must be treated as execution-boundary changes, not ordinary source-only refactors.

Located InvestigationRepository, InvestigationAdoptionPolicy, CanonicalReviewWorkAdapter and assessReviewCompletion. Existing sc1-sc7 owners already provide scope, typed evidence, ledger validation, durable block acceptance, ownership and canonical completion. S7 consumes the public integration boundary and corrects its private wiring; it does not implement replacement versions of those shared contracts.

Prior offline replay of the real acceptance manifest reproduced three invalid old-side references for insertion-only spans; the live trace showed serial reads and no progress call. Test lookup was off-topic; direct search located existing backend bridge, evidence, adoption/recovery and build TESTS writer tests.
